slides.body:
Bibimbap is old. Bibimbap as a thing you order in a restaurant is not, and Korean food writing keeps pointing at the same few doors in Jeonju.

This is one of them. Korean press describes it as opening in Gyeongwon-dong in 1952, mid-war, taking a dish people assembled at home from leftovers and putting it on a printed menu. It is still a family business, on its third generation, and per Wikipedia it makes its own gochujang, soy sauce and sesame oil rather than buying them in.

On the recognition: it appeared in the Michelin Green Guide Korea in 2011 — the travel guide, not the starred restaurant guide. Worth separating, because the two get quoted interchangeably. Korean coverage also notes a run of presidents eating here on visits to Jeonju, and the family's Seoul branches still list a 'President bibimbap'.

Those branches are the other thing to know. The Seoul operation sits in department stores and towers and charges roughly 22,000 won for the same bowl. The Jeonju room is the original, and cheaper.
